app.notice: Risk measurement tool. Not investment advice.
app.title: VaR and Expected Shortfall for Brazilian portfolios
backtest.chart_caption: The line is the predicted limit. Crosses mark violations, days when the loss went past it. Gray bands are crisis periods.
backtest.summary: We compare what each estimator predicted with what happened afterwards, separately in calm and in crisis periods.
compare.chart_caption: Each group shows the next-day loss predicted by one estimator. CAViaR has no ES.
compare.chart_title: VaR and ES by estimator, in R$
compare.steps: Step by step, with your portfolio's numbers
compare.summary: Each estimator is a different way of measuring the same risk. Large differences mean the risk is hard to pin down.
data.chart_caption: Shows how the portfolio would have grown with constant weights, dividends included and no costs.
data.chart_title: Value of R$ 100 invested in the portfolio
data.corrections: Corrections: {filled} short gaps filled, {stale} days without trades ignored, {inconsistent} inconsistent prices discarded and {breaks} artificial jumps removed.
data.more_cleaning: Days without trades and inconsistent prices count as gaps. Gaps of up to {days} days repeat the last price, and longer ones stay empty. Days when any asset has no return are left out.
data.more_extreme: Large daily moves kept and flagged for review: {items}.
data.more_limits: Yahoo Finance is not an official source. Using stocks listed today favours companies that survived.
data.more_no_extreme: No daily move above the review limit in these assets.
data.summary: Prices come from Yahoo Finance, extraction of {as_of}, covering {first} to {last} ({days} days of portfolio returns).
download.button: Download CSV with all forecasts and tests
download.caption: The file uses English column names, so results are the same in both languages.
error.amount: The amount invested must be greater than zero.
error.download: Could not download the prices. Try again in a few minutes.
error.duplicate: Each ticker can appear only once.
error.too_short: This portfolio has {days} days of common history. At least {needed} are needed.

estimator.caviar.assumptions: The quantile follows an asymmetric autoregressive rule, and no return distribution is assumed.
estimator.caviar.limitations: Gives no ES, and the fit is a non-convex search that may not reach the global optimum.
estimator.caviar.name: CAViaR
estimator.caviar.step1: Fitted parameters for α = {alpha}: β1 = {beta1}, β2 = {beta2}, β3 = {beta3}, β4 = {beta4}.
estimator.caviar.summary: Models the loss limit directly, reacting differently to rises and falls. It gives VaR only.
estimator.evt_pot.assumptions: Excesses over a high threshold follow a generalized Pareto distribution, with ξ below 1.
estimator.evt_pot.limitations: The threshold balances bias and variance, and the fit can be unstable in short windows.
estimator.evt_pot.name: Extreme value theory (POT)
estimator.evt_pot.step1: GARCH parameters: μ = {mu}, ω = {omega}, a = {a}, b = {b}. Volatility forecast: σ = {sigma_next}.
estimator.evt_pot.step2: Threshold u = {u}, the 90% quantile of standardized losses: {n_u} of {n} observations lie above it.
estimator.evt_pot.step3: Generalized Pareto fit to those excesses: ξ = {xi}, β = {beta}.
estimator.evt_pot.step4: Standardized loss quantile for α = {alpha}: y = {y_alpha}, so VaR = {var_pct} ({var_brl}).
estimator.evt_pot.summary: Uses today's volatility from GARCH and fits a curve made for extreme losses.
estimator.fhs.assumptions: GARCH volatility, with residuals that are independent and identically distributed.
estimator.fhs.limitations: The residual quantile still depends on few observations in the extreme tail.
estimator.fhs.name: Filtered historical simulation
estimator.fhs.step1: GARCH parameters: μ = {mu}, ω = {omega}, a = {a}, b = {b}. Persistence {persistence}, half-life {half_life} days.
estimator.fhs.step2: Volatility forecast for the next day: σ = {sigma_next}.
estimator.fhs.step3: {n} returns divided by their volatility give the residuals. For α = {alpha}, k = {k}.
estimator.fhs.step4: The k-th worst residual is {quantile}, so VaR = {var_pct} ({var_brl}).
estimator.fhs.step5: The mean of the k worst residuals is {tail_mean}, so ES = {es_pct} ({es_brl}).
estimator.fhs.summary: Uses today's volatility from GARCH and takes the shape of bad days from history.
estimator.garch_t.assumptions: GARCH(1,1) volatility with symmetric Student t innovations, fitted by maximum likelihood.
estimator.garch_t.limitations: The symmetric t does not capture skewed tails, and results depend on the quality of the fit.
estimator.garch_t.name: GARCH-t
estimator.garch_t.step1: Fitted parameters: μ = {mu}, ω = {omega}, a = {a}, b = {b}, ν = {nu}.
estimator.garch_t.step2: Persistence a + b = {persistence}: half of a shock fades in {half_life} days. Long-run daily volatility: {long_run_volatility}.
estimator.garch_t.step3: Volatility forecast for the next day: σ = {sigma_next}.
estimator.garch_t.step4: Unit-variance t quantile for α = {alpha}: {quantile}, so VaR = {var_pct} ({var_brl}).
estimator.garch_t.step5: Tail mean of the same distribution: {tail_mean}, so ES = {es_pct} ({es_brl}).
estimator.garch_t.summary: Lets volatility change every day and allows for more extreme days than a bell curve.
estimator.hs.assumptions: All days in the window weigh the same, and the future looks like the window.
estimator.hs.limitations: Reacts late to new shocks and jumps when an old shock leaves the window. Depends on few observations.
estimator.hs.name: Historical simulation
estimator.hs.step1: Window of {n} returns, sorted from worst to best. For α = {alpha}, k = {k}.
estimator.hs.step2: The k-th worst return is {quantile}, so VaR = {var_pct} ({var_brl}).
estimator.hs.step3: The mean of the k worst returns is {tail_mean}, so ES = {es_pct} ({es_brl}).
estimator.hs.summary: Assumes tomorrow looks like the last 1000 days and reads the risk directly from the worst days.
estimator.normal.assumptions: Normal returns with constant mean and volatility inside the window.
estimator.normal.limitations: Ignores heavy tails and changing volatility. Tends to underestimate risk in a crisis.
estimator.normal.name: Normal
estimator.normal.step2: For α = {alpha}, the normal quantile is z = {z_alpha}, so VaR = {var_pct} ({var_brl}).
estimator.normal.step3: The standard normal tail mean is {tail_mean}, so ES = {es_pct} ({es_brl}).
estimator.normal.summary: The simplest baseline: assumes returns follow a bell curve with constant volatility.
input.help: Enter B3 tickers and weights. Weights must sum to 1.
input.running: Downloading prices and backtesting the six estimators. This takes about a minute.
input.start_hint: Review the portfolio and press the button to start.
light.chart_caption: The dashed lines separate the zones: up to 4 violations is green, 5 to 9 is yellow, and 10 or more is red.
light.summary: {estimator} is in the {zone} zone, with {count} violations in the last 250 days.
light.too_short: There are fewer than 250 forecast days, so the traffic light is not available.
main.chart_caption: Each bar counts days with that return. The lines mark the VaR 99% and the ES 97.5% of the recommended estimator.
main.chart_title: Daily returns of the portfolio, last {days} days
main.es_missing: The recommended estimator does not give an Expected Shortfall.
main.es_reading: On the worst {tail}% of days, the average expected loss is {amount} ({percent}).
main.horizon: These numbers are for the next trading day.
main.more_limits: One-day horizon, constant weights, no transaction costs and no derivatives.
main.more_reference: McNeil, Frey and Embrechts (2015); Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (2019).
main.more_regime: A day is a crisis day when the Ibovespa's 21-day volatility on the previous day is above the 80th percentile of its whole history up to then.
main.more_regime_value: Regime expected for the next trading day: {regime}.
main.more_var_es: VaR is the loss that should be exceeded only with probability α. ES is the average loss when that happens.
main.var_reading: On {days} out of 100 days, the portfolio is not expected to lose more than {amount} ({percent}).
recommend.reason.caviar_only: Only {estimator} passed the tests in {regime} periods. It estimates VaR only, so there is no reliable ES here. Failed the tests: {rejected}.
recommend.reason.none_passed: No estimator passed all tests in {regime} periods. {estimator} is the least bad: it failed the fewest tests and, among those, had the lowest loss. Failed the tests: {rejected}.
recommend.reason.passed: {estimator} passed the reliability tests in {regime} periods and had the lowest loss among those that passed. Failed the tests: {rejected}.
recommend.warning_low_power: Warning: there are few days in this regime, so the tests can miss real problems.
recommend.warning_none: Warning: treat these numbers with care, because no estimator was approved for this regime.
test.christoffersen.assumptions: Violations follow a first-order Markov chain. Pairs of days that are not neighbours inside a regime are not counted.
test.christoffersen.limitations: Only detects dependence on the previous day.
test.christoffersen.summary: Checks the frequency of violations and whether they come in clusters.
test.dm.assumptions: The variance is estimated with Newey-West to allow for autocorrelation.
test.dm.limitations: CAViaR has no ES, so it is compared on quantile loss only.
test.dm.summary: Checks whether the difference in loss between two estimators is statistically significant.
test.fz0.assumptions: VaR and ES are positive losses, so v and e are negative in the formula.
test.fz0.limitations: Ranks estimators but does not say whether any of them is adequate.
test.fz0.reference: Fissler and Ziegel (2016); Patton, Ziegel and Chen (2019).
test.fz0.summary: Scores VaR and ES together to rank estimators. Lower is better.
test.kupiec.assumptions: Violations are independent with a fixed probability under the null hypothesis.
test.kupiec.limitations: Says nothing about when violations occur or how large they are.
test.kupiec.summary: Checks whether violations happen as often as promised.
test.z2.assumptions: The p-value is simulated from each day's predicted tail, with 1000 replications and a fixed seed.
test.z2.limitations: One-sided: it does not flag an overestimated ES.
test.z2.summary: Checks the frequency and the size of losses beyond VaR together. Low p-values mean ES was underestimated.
tests.care: Tests have low power with few violations and ignore estimation error, so prefer large and consistent differences.
tests.dm_caption: A negative statistic favours the first estimator. Differences matter when p is below 0.05. Regime: {regime}.
tests.summary: A p-value of 0.05 or more means the test found no problem. Results below that are marked as failed.
